Release status

OpenTDCR is a release candidate prepared from the supplied hardware and teleoperation project. The public source tree is a separate, curated export; the original working project is preserved.

Included in this candidate

  • An installable Python package with a default dry-run path, explicit physical-hardware opt-in, configurable tendon kinematics, sensor-independent calibration, and measurement adapters including optional Lyra.
  • The original assembly STEP and seven individual STL files, plus a hash manifest and a BOM worksheet.
  • Hardware, setup, configuration, calibration-boundary, architecture, and contributor documentation.
  • Unit tests using simulated transports; these do not exercise physical actuators.
  • A CAD explorer generated from the supplied assembly, and a clearly labeled constant-curvature shape illustration.

Hardware correspondence

The STEP contains the actuation unit and mounts, including commercial component geometry. The flexible backbone is not modeled. The standalone STL files predate this STEP export; revision correspondence and completeness are not yet established.

The sixteen modeled servo housings are a CAD inventory observation, not a verified tendon count. The nine-tendon software example is illustrative. A maintainer must supply the actual servo map, geometry, backbone specifications, routing, and limits.

Licenses and attribution

Software uses the MIT license with Continuum Robotics Laboratory, University of Toronto attribution (2026), preserving the inherited Chengnan Shentu notice (2024). A hardware license has not been selected. Embedded supplier CAD and reference-image rights require review before a public hardware release. The candidate does not claim that every CAD component is already open licensed.

Required physical validation

Test the new hardware path with the target servo firmware and an operator present: startup, signed motion, travel limits, readback, shutdown, communication failures, and reference establishment. Test a real sensor adapter for units, frame orientation, acquisition timing, and tracking loss.

Teleoperation uses measurements as an availability gate. The separate calibration command preserves the lab’s displacement-threshold/countback sequence through a generic sensor interface. It establishes position references rather than measuring tendon force, and acknowledges Lee et al., ICRA 2025. The refactored calibration and optional Lyra adapter require physical validation.

Publication decisions

Complete the hardware license and attribution review, finish the BOM and missing geometry, and record the bench results before announcing a reproducible open-hardware release. The repository’s docs/release-checklist.md is the working checklist.

Research sources

The companion paper and simulator remain separate artifacts: paper and authors, project and physics demo, and simulation source. The supplied assembly’s exact correspondence to the paper hardware remains to be documented.
